text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.05% today to $142.38, continuing a sharp two-week rally that's added nearly 14% to the stock price. The immediate driver is escalating geopolitical tension in the Middle East—container ships are being attacked in the Strait of Hormuz, Saudi Aramco facilities have been struck, and Iran is stepping up its campaign against commercial shipping. These supply disruptions are pushing crude oil prices higher (world oil at $125.44/barrel, up sharply), which benefits an oil producer like ConocoPhillips.

The broader backdrop making this move stick is a real supply crunch, not just headline risk. The International Energy Agency warned today that diesel specifically will remain in tight supply well into 2027 due to the Iran conflict, falling inventories, and strong demand—meaning prices for refined products and crude are likely to stay elevated. This transforms the geopolitical crisis from a one-day news spike into a structural headwind for global energy supply, which typically supports producers' margins and stock prices over weeks or months.
